coverage.note: lecturesTotal is the 9 recorded lectures in the Cairn catalog on 2026-10-21; the course site schedules 24, of which 1-9 had videos and slides. All nine are covered: Lectures 1 (the introduction), 2 (discrete motion planning), 3 (randomized motion planning with RRTs), 4 (quadrotor dynamics), 5 (differential flatness), 6 (trajectory optimization), 7 (stability and PD control), 8 (the linear quadratic regulator) and 9 (optical flow).

notes.note: The LaTeX notes of Lectures 4 (7 pages, equations (1)-(32)), 5 (4 pages, equations (1)-(4)), 6 (3 pages, equations (1)-(10), no figures), 7 (5 pages, equations (1)-(19), three drawings), 8 (4 pages, one numbered equation (1), two drawings) and 9 (5 pages, equations (1)-(5), four drawings) are transcribed to raw/notes/ (full text, equations in LaTeX under the notes' own numbers, figures described), read from page images like the decks. They carry each lecture's derivation, which was done on a blackboard not visible in the video.

caveats: Covers all 9 recorded lectures (lectures 1-9). The course site schedules 24; lectures 10 onward had not been posted, so the KB cannot answer questions about their technical content (the nondeterministic filter onward).
Transcripts are copy-edited from YouTube auto-captions; a few passages in each lecture were too garbled to restore and are marked [Ed: unclear]. The verbatim captions are not committed.
Lecture 1's deck has no slide 2 (hidden before export): slide N is PDF page N-1 from slide 3 on. Citations use the printed numbers.
Lecture 2's slide 73 says a tie in F is 'broken by smaller H', but both tied vertices have H = 6; the lecturer notices this in class (≈1:06:47). The slide file and wiki page say so.
Lecture 2's slides 62 and 76 are animations in the lecture; the PDF, and the image of slide 76, hold a single early frame.

Lecture 3's slides 49, 50, 58 and 59 are animations or videos; the PDF holds single frames (50 part-grown, 58 and 59 identical opening frames), so the wiki describes them as the lecture narrates them.

Lecture 4's derivation was written on a blackboard that the video does not show; the wiki reconstructs the equations from the lecture notes, cited by the notes' own equation numbers, and says where the lecture's pointing cannot be resolved.
Lecture 4's notes contain printed slips (a wrong figure reference, ≜ in eq. (28), a stray parenthesis) and elide most of eq. (30); raw/notes/ keeps them as printed and lists them.

Lecture 5's derivation was also done on the blackboard; the wiki follows the notes, whose equation numbers (1)-(4) match the ones spoken. The moment equation was first written with F1 + F2 and corrected in class to F2 - F1 (the notes print F2 - F1).

Lecture 5's slides 3-6 are videos; the PDF holds one frame of each and slide 5's is black, so the wiki describes the videos as the lecture narrates them. Two research-group heads named aloud (Davide Scaramuzza, Sertac Karaman) are restored from garbled captions and printed nowhere in the course material.

Lecture 6's derivation (linearization, the A and B matrices, the quadratic program) was also done on the blackboard; the wiki follows the notes, whose equation numbers (1)-(10) the lecture never speaks. On the board the velocities were v_x, v_y, omega and the constraint matrix C was k by n; the notes write x-dot, y-dot, theta-dot and give C as n by n. Slides 14 and 16-18 hold single frames of a demo and videos shown in class; slide 3's video frame is black. 'Claude', named aloud as the tool the slide 14 demo was made with, is restored from the captions' 'cloud' and printed nowhere in the course material.

Lecture 7's definitions and PD example were also done on the blackboard; the wiki follows the notes, whose equation numbers (1)-(19) the lecture never speaks. The board defines global and local attractivity and builds asymptotic stability from them plus stability in the sense of Lyapunov; the notes fold the convergence condition into their definitions of asymptotic stability. The notes' eq. (16) prints the proportional gain as k_p/m, inconsistent with eqs. (13) and (17) and with the board; the wiki uses k_p(y - y_0) and says so. Slide 3 holds the first frame of a simulation run in class; the deviations it showed are from the lecture.

Lecture 8's LQR formulation was also done on the blackboard; the wiki follows the notes, which number only one equation, (1), and are otherwise cited by page. The notes state no derivation (the lecture skips it), print 'Riccatti' for Riccati and give the positive-definite condition 'for all x', which the lecture corrects to all non-zero vectors (≈29:09). Slide 8 repeats the k_p/m of the Lecture 7 notes' eq. (16); spoken, the controller has k_p(y - y_0). Slides 11-13 hold single frames of videos played in class, slide 13's being only the title card. A second person named as having tuned the lab's Q and R is garbled in the captions and left unclear.

Lecture 9's derivation (brightness constancy, the aperture problem, Lucas-Kanade) was also done on the blackboard; the wiki follows the notes, whose equations (1)-(3) the lecture calls equations one to three and whose (4)-(5) it does not number. The lecture calls the first assumption intensity constancy, the notes color and intensity (or brightness) constancy. The captions garble the spoken least-squares solution and the student answer naming the edge case; the wiki uses the notes. At one point the lecture describes the edge failure as motion 'aligned with the image gradients', where the notes' derivation makes it motion perpendicular to them; the wiki says so. Slides 5, 12, 15 and 19 hold single frames of videos played in class (slide 12's is black) and slide 11 only a link. The notes' page-1 header prints 'Lecture #18', and a drawing labels a displaced point '(x+u, x+v)'.
